# iliad-036 (6.1–115) — review, pass 1 (units only; gloss.json not yet present)

`t` was checked against the archive (joined text identical) and never touched. Line breaks of `l` agree with `t` in all 60 units. Paragraph marks (`p`) fall on units at 1, 5, 12, 20, 29, 37, 51, 61, 66, 72, 102 as the edition prints. Quotation marks: five speeches (Adrastus 46–50, Agamemnon 55–60, Nestor 67–71, Helenus 77–101, Hector 111–115), each with `mark` and “ on its first unit and ” on its last, in both `l` and `i`; iliad-035 ends at 5.909 with no speech open, so nothing runs in. The two repeated-line cases with the Odyssey and earlier Iliad parts (6.9–11, 6.48, 6.67, 6.72, 6.103–106) carry the published English unchanged. Scan flag, line 45: scanned by hand (Ἄδρη | στος δ’ ἄρ’ ἔ | πει τα λα | βὼν ἐ | λίσ σε το | γού νων); the line only scans if the ἐ- of ἐλίσσετο counts long in the biceps of foot 4, so the irregularity is real and the unit's existing note already says so in one sentence; no change needed. Table rows consulted: κρείων, ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν, ἐξενάριξε, οὖτα, ἔπεφνε, ἐνήρατο, ἕλε, κέκλετο, ἀρηΐφιλος, ἠΰκομος, γλαυκῶπις, μείλινον, πέπον, νήπια τέκνα, ἀπερείσια ἄποινα, μήστωρ φόβοιο, οἰωνοπόλων ὄχ’ ἄριστος, φύλοπις αἰνή, θούριδος ἀλκῆς, ἐλελίχθησαν, ὄρχαμος, ὑπέρθυμος, ἐπίκουρος.

## Changes (line · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

Line numbers are the unit's `ln`.

1. 49 (6.96) · n · **major** · The note said μήστωρα φόβοιο "is used of Diomedes’s horses at 5.272". Checked against the source: 5.272 is τὼ δὲ δύ’ Αἰνείᾳ δῶκεν μήστωρε φόβοιο, the pair of horses Anchises gave to Aeneas. · Note now says the same words are used at 5.272 of the pair of horses Anchises gave to Aeneas.
2. 49 · l · moderate · "strong master of flight": the table fixes μήστωρ φόβοιο as "counsellors of flight" in `l`, "masters of flight" in `i` (4.328, 5.272); new-renderings.md claims the table row is reused unchanged. · `l` now "strong counsellor of flight"; `i` ("master of flight") already right.
3. 52 (6.100–101) · n · moderate · Label wrong: οἱ called "‘his’, a dative of possession". ἰσοφαρίζω takes the dative of the person matched and an accusative of respect (21.411 μοι μένος ἰσοφαρίζεις; 21.194 and 9.390 dative), so οἱ is "him" and μένος is "in might". · Note rewritten (οἱ ‘him’, dative with ἰσοφαρίζειν; μένος accusative of respect).
4. 52 · l, i · moderate · "match his might" followed the wrong construction. · `l` "no one is able to match him in might"; `i` "no one can match him in might".
5. 41 (6.77–80) · n · moderate · Τρώων καὶ Λυκίων called "a genitive of the whole group"; it is the partitive genitive with μάλιστα ("on you most of all the Trojans and Lycians"). · Label corrected.
6. 41 · i · moderate · "the labour of all the Trojans and Lycians rests most heavily on you" read the genitive as the owner of the toil, not as the group from which Aeneas and Hector are singled out; it also disagreed with `l`. · `i` now "since the labour rests most heavily on you, of all the Trojans and Lycians,".
7. 17 (6.35) · i · moderate · "caught Phylacus": the table's avoided words for ἕλε/ἕλεν in killing (5.37) are "captured", "caught", and the note says this ἕλε is a killing in contrast to the capture at 38 (ζωὸν ἕλ’). `i` contradicted the note. · `i` "killed Phylacus as he fled" (`l` keeps "took").
8. 20 (6.38–41) · l, i · moderate · "where the others too": nothing in the Greek is "too"; the note's "just where" for ᾗ περ was not in either layer. · `l` "just where the others, dazed with fear, were fleeing"; `i` "just where the rest were fleeing, dazed with fear,".
9. 15 (6.32–33) · l · minor · ἐνήρατο is "slew" in `l` (table, 5.43; shipped iliad-027), unit had "killed". · "slew".
10. 40 (6.73–76) · l · minor · "There, indeed, again": "indeed" corresponds to nothing (κεν is modal, already shown by "would have gone up"; compare iliad-008, 2.155). · "There, again,".
11. 1 (6.2–4) · i · minor · "surged this way and that" is not what ἴθυσε (‘rushed straight on’, so the note) says and reads as remembered English. · "rushed here and there".
12. 5 (6.15) · i · minor · φιλέεσκεν is the iterative (the note says ‘used to love’), `i` "loved" lost it. · "for he used to love them all".
13. 7 (6.19) · i · minor · "went down into the earth": ‘down’ is not in the Greek (γαῖαν ἐδύτην, ‘entered the earth’, as `l`) and the phrase is the stock English for it. · "and the two of them entered the earth."
14. 11 (6.25) · i · minor · "lay with her in love" dropped εὐνῇ and the verb's force (μίγη ‘was joined’). · "he joined with her in love and in bed".
15. 31 (6.57–60) · l · minor · "nor let him escape" turned the relative μηδ’ ὃς φύγοι into a main clause. · "nor who might escape".
16. 37 (6.67–70) · i · minor · "hang back, intent on the spoils" for μιμνέτω … ἐπιβαλλόμενος: `l`/note say ‘stay behind’, ‘throwing himself upon’. · "let no one now stay behind, throwing himself on the spoils so as to reach the ships carrying the most;".
17. 38 (6.70–71) · n · minor · Note glossed ἂμ πεδίον ‘up and down the plain’; `l` has "along", `i` "across"; ἀνὰ πεδίον is simply ‘over the plain’. · ‘along, over the plain’.
18. 44 (6.85) · n · minor · "ἀναγκαίη is ἀνάγκη with the epic ending -η": the ending is not what differs; it is the longer epic form. · "the longer epic form".

## Findings considered and refused

- 23 (6.45), scansion: real irregularity, already stated in the unit's note in one sentence (ἐ- of ἐλίσσετο counts long in foot 4). Nothing to add.
- 29 (6.55) `i` "these men" where the Greek has only ἀνδρῶν: English cannot say "for men" here; the note says the men are the Trojans. Kept.
- 29 (6.55) "My good fellow" while the note says the sense of πέπον is not known: this is the table's exact pairing (5.109, 2.235). Kept.
- 20 `i` "were caught in a tamarisk branch" for βλαφθέντε (`l` "hindered"): natural English for the sense, no wording recalled; kept.
- 27 (6.52–53) `i` "to be led down" for active καταξέμεν (the attendant leads): the shift of voice keeps the English clear and the note says "lead down". Kept. The note does not say the infinitive is future; the form label "-έμεν (= Attic -ειν)" is true as given.
- 51 (6.100) `i` "though they say" for ὅν πέρ φασι: concessive πέρ, supported by the note ("extra weight"); kept.
- 56 (6.107) "under its third name": ambiguous but not false (Ἀργεῖοι is one of the three names, as unit 36's note says). Kept.
- 56 (6.109) `i` "seeing how they had wheeled round" for ὡς ἐλέλιχθεν: the causal reading is the one the note commits to; kept.
- 43 (6.84) `i` drops "even" of καὶ μάλα … περ ("badly worn down"): force is carried by "badly … though". Kept.
- 35, 34, 36, 57, 53 and the other short units: all labels, positions and cross-references (1.69, 1.500, 2.110, 2.873, 4.208, 5.347, 5.439, 5.470, 5.494–497, 5.907–909, lines 12, 21, 33, 35, 38, 44, 55, 64, 66, 73–74, 78, 86, 87–95, 98, 101, 102, 110, 112) verified true against the source and the lines; no change.
- The new-renderings.md rows were read against `l`/`i` in the units; each row agrees with the unit it names (no change to rows needed; row for μήστωρ is a reuse and the unit is now in line with it).

# Pass 2 (gloss) — gloss.json read against the lines

Scope: all 185 entries and the 22 `__broaden__` entries of `gloss.json` checked against the line, `novel-forms.json`, `known-forms.json` and the notes in `units.json`. Format checked by script: every entry under 230 characters (broadened entries are longer by construction), no ASCII apostrophe or backtick, no line numbers, no "here"; every `__broaden__` value is the known entry whole + ` · ` + new reading, and every key exists in `known-forms.json`; gloss keys equal `novel-forms.json` exactly; every token of `t` is covered by a gloss, a known key or a broadened key. Known entries not broadened were read against each place they occur (πὰρ δέ οἱ ἔστη, ὁδῷ ἔπι, ἐπεί κε, ᾧ θεράποντι, ὃν δή, ἣ δέ, κατὰ λαπάρην, and the rest): all covered.

## Changes (form · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. σκότιον · moderate · Entry parsed it "masc. acc. sg., predicative", but the unit's note (6.24) calls it "neuter, used as an adverb"; the two contradicted each other. · Entry now "neut. acc. sg. used as an adverb: ’in secret’".
2. χάρμα (`__broaden__`) · minor · New reading said "neut. nom. sg., predicate after γενέσθαι"; the subject of γενέσθαι in 6.80 is λαόν/φεύγοντας (accusative), so the predicate is accusative. · Reading now "neut. acc. sg., predicate after γενέσθαι: ’a joy’" (old entry untouched).
3. πεπύθοιτ · minor · Attic equivalent given as ἐπύθετο (an indicative); the form is an optative, whose Attic equivalent is πύθοιτο. · "Attic πύθοιτο".
4. ἠκέστας · minor · Lemma written ἠκεστός (oxytone), which would give fem. acc. pl. ἠκεστάς; the printed ἠκέστας is paroxytone and can only come from proparoxytone ἤκεστος. · Lemma now ἤκεστος (?); the "sense not certain" caveat kept, as the unit's note has it.
5. ἴθυσε · minor · English gloss ’rushed, surged’ kept "surged", the very word pass 1 removed from the unit as not what ἴθυσε says. · ’rushed on’.

## Findings considered and refused

- ὔμμι "epic encl.": the form is printed with an accent and the note calls it "the Aeolic form"; but the entry is word for word the published odyssey-glossary entry (first entry to land stands). Kept.
- οἴξασα lemma οἴγω against the note's οἴγνυμι: both are LSJ lemmas, and the published glossaries use both. Kept.
- δαμέντες lemma δάμνημι against the note's δαμάζω: the published glossaries use both for the same forms. Kept.
- πέρ (`__broaden__`) "intensive … ’whom indeed’" for ὅν πέρ φασι, against pass 1's "though they say": the known entry already gives "concessive or intensive", and the unit's note says only "extra weight"; the new reading is true and the old entry whole covers the other. Kept.
- οἰκία "Homer has only neut. pl.": a statement about the whole poem, but it is the lexical fact LSJ gives (οἰκίον, only pl. in Homer) and says nothing about this part beyond the line. Kept.
- δύναται, μάχεσθαί, κήδεαι etc. "pres. 3 sg./inf." without "mid." for deponents: not wrong, same as published entries. Kept.
- ἀναγκαίη "ἀναγκαῖος … as a noun": the note calls it "ἀνάγκη, the longer epic form"; both say the same thing (necessity, nom. sg.). Kept.
- All remaining parses (case, number, tense, mood, voice, augment, duals βλαφθέντε / ἀτυζομένω / ἄξαντ’ / ἐβήτην / ἐδύτην / ἐποτρύνητον, elisions, Attic equivalents, the Πήδασον homograph, article-forms, ᾧ possessive) verified against the lines and left unchanged.
